purpose: Rights-aware follow-up actions for Wave 8 longitudinal mould-maintenance evidence. The goal is to turn public aggregate findings into Book-owned lifecycle teaching structures while separately pursuing authorized raw histories.

queue.action: create an original event-schema and example timeline showing mould ID -> shot count -> component maintenance notification -> next maintenance interval, using only public aggregate/source-described fields; clearly mark component condition and post-maintenance part-quality verification as unavailable in the public record
queue.artifactTarget: shot-count mould-maintenance history timeline + maintenance-event data schema

queue.action: pursue owner-authorized access to a de-identified subset of maintenance notifications/master data, prioritizing repeated event sequences for the same mould/component and explicit separation of cleaning, repair and replacement events

build a Book-owned case matrix from the disclosed mould age, cycles/week, cavities, issue/failure attributes and maintenance-time ranges; use it to teach similarity-based planning without reproducing the source table

stillWanted: a rights-clear longitudinal injection-mould maintenance dataset with repeated events for the same mould/component plus explicit intervention type and post-maintenance condition
part-quality/metrology measurements immediately before and after natural mould maintenance or refurbishment, linked to the same maintenance event history
rights-clear shot-by-shot black-speck onset -> intervention -> verified-recovery data with part order/timestamps and process state
synchronized hot-runner actual valve-pin position + motor current/torque + cavity pressure + cavity-specific quality traces
gapUpdate: Long natural maintenance histories are no longer an evidence-discovery gap: a 2011-2024 industrial history with 64,020 notifications across 9,157 moulds is now identified. The remaining gap is access/reuse plus physical condition and verified post-maintenance quality recovery linked to those events.
